newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan stocks close firm, investors cautious.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan stocks close firm, investors cautious.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks closed firm on Monday but investors were cautious after nearly three weeks of a slow but steady rise in the all share index, brokers said.
The all share index closed 0.87 points higher at 593.20.
"Investors are cautiously watching the index to see where it will go from here," said K. Anurathan of CDIC Sasoon Cumberbatch Stock Brokers.
The index rose nearly 14 points in the first half of last week, but flattened out in the last two days making investors nervous that the market may have lost steam, he said.

Turnover was a thin 7.4 million rupees on 529,495 shares. Foreign purchases were 1.9 million rupees and sales 2.4 million. "Foreign interest is still there. But foreign buying takes place only when there is selling in bulk," said Ralph Wijesinghe of Asia Securities.
The privatisation of 51 percent, or 4.8 million shares, in Udapussellawa Plantations at 65.25 rupees a 10-rupee share enlivened an otherswise dull day, brokers said.
They said the price, highest per-share price for any state-owned plantation firm, augured well for listed plantation shares. -- Prithi kodagoda (941) 434319
